group:paper-gaokao-2021-i:seven-choices.overview: 作者带着自嘲写一周巴黎生活：想像本地人那样过日子，租下又小又贵的公寓；巴黎人吃美食不长胖，因为好吃一点就够、水果又贵；咖啡馆满座和每周35小时工作制说明法国人重生活质量。
group:paper-gaokao-2021-i:seven-choices.fullTranslationZh:
我和丈夫刚在巴黎住了一周。我们的目标是看看能否在某种程度上像真正的巴黎人那样生活。因此，第一件事就是租下一套贵得惊人、只有橱柜大小的六楼公寓。它太小了，我们不得不把行李箱放在走廊。

不过，这地方也不完全地道。和通常的巴黎公寓不同，这里的水管能正常工作。有一间不错的厨房和一张舒适的床。楼里甚至有一部小电梯，用完美的法语女声说“门正在打开”。这是我唯一学会的法语，可惜平时用不上几次。

巴黎人和你我不同。他们从不显得懒散或邋遢。正如几周前有人在本报所说，他们吃着美食却从不长胖。食物实在太美味，只需吃一点就能感到满足。法国草莓不像硬纸板；相反，它们在口中像一颗颗小小的味觉炸弹一样迸发滋味。

这并不是法国人比我们吃得少的唯一原因。到巴黎的第一个早晨，我绕过街角去食品市场采购。我买了一小把完全成熟的小草莓和一只小甜瓜。丈夫和我都觉得这是我们吃过的最好吃的水果。但它们竟要18美元！

在法国，生活质量比效率重要得多。

从咖啡馆生活就能看出来。法国咖啡馆总是挤满人。并非所有顾客都是游客。这些人什么时候工作呢？法国人认真对待每周35小时工作制，认真到一些工会最近与一批公司达成协议，限制独立承包者随时待命的小时数。

completedSourceTexts.text: My husband and I just spent a week in Paris. Our aim was to see if we could live, in some way, like real Parisians. So the first thing we did was rent a fantastically expensive sixth-floor apartment the size of a cupboard. It was so tiny that we had to leave our suitcases in the hallway.

The place wasn’t entirely authentic, though. Unlike a normal Parisian apartment, the plumbing (水管) worked. There was a nice kitchen and a comfortable bed. Our building even had a tiny lift with a female voice that said, “Ouverture des portes,” in perfect French. That is the only French phrase I mastered, and it’s a shame I don’t have much use for it.

Parisians are different from you and me. They never look lazy or untidy. As someone noted in this paper a couple of weeks ago, they eat great food and never gain weight. The food is so delicious that you don’t need much of it to make you happy. French strawberries do not taste like cardboard. Instead, they explode in your mouth like little flavor bombs.

That’s not the only reason the French eat less than we do. On our first morning in Paris, I went around the corner to the food market to pick up some groceries. I bought a handful of perfectly ripe small strawberries and a little sweet melon. My husband and I agreed they were the best fruit we had ever eaten. But they cost $18!

You can tell this by café life. French cafés are always crowded. Not all the customers are tourists. When do these people work? The French take their 35-hour workweek seriously – so seriously that some labor unions recently struck a deal with a group of companies limiting the number of hours that independent contractors can be on call.
